title: Vau calculus, explained
h1: Vau calculus: fexprs with a real equational theory, because evaluation is explicit
lead: In Lisp, a fexpr is a first-class combiner that receives its operands unevaluated. Mitchell Wand showed in 1998 that if a calculus makes evaluation implicit (every reduction is evaluation), then adding fexprs makes its theory of contextual equivalence trivial. John N. Shutt's vau calculi avoid this by making evaluation explicit: a term [eval T] asks for evaluation, and the operand T alone is just data. This site explains the pure vau-x calculus (Shutt's thesis, section 9.3): its syntax, its values, and its seven general reduction rules. No Lean exists yet. Every node is marked PLAN: it explains the theory from the sources and claims nothing is proved.
desc: Unofficial, AI-drafted plain-English explainer of John N. Shutt's vau calculus: why explicit evaluation, the pure vau-x syntax, and the reduction rules eval-self, eval-pair, eval-wrap, combine-wrap, beta-vau, parse-nil and parse-pair. A Lean 4 formalization is planned; none exists yet.

startNote: All definitions here follow Shutt's PhD thesis (WPI, 2010), chapter 9: the pure vau-x calculus of section 9.3, and, only to make $vau understandable, the environment calculus vau-e of section 9.1. Notation is written in plain ASCII: [eval T], [combine T1 T2], <T> for an applicative, and <vau x.T>, <vau0.T>, <vau2.T> for the three compound operatives. The rule names (eval-self and so on) are this project's names for Shutt's schemata (9.25S), (9.25p), (9.25a), (9.25gamma), (9.25beta), (9.25vau0) and (9.25vau2).

aboutCreditMd:
## Credit, licence and status

- **The theory:** the vau calculi are the work of [John N. Shutt](https://web.cs.wpi.edu/~jshutt/), in his PhD thesis *Fexprs as the basis of Lisp function application; or, $vau: the ultimate abstraction* (Worcester Polytechnic Institute, 2010) and his 2007 NEPLS talk. The actor view of Kernel is from Dale Schumacher's posts. The triviality result is from Mitchell Wand, *The Theory of Fexprs is Trivial* (Lisp and Symbolic Computation, 1998).
- **This explainer:** unofficial and independent. Drafted by Claude (AI) at the request of the repository owner. No person has reviewed it, and the cited authors have not seen it. It may contain errors. Every node is `review: draft`.
- **Lean:** none yet. When Lean lands in this repository, the node statuses will change from PLAN to proved or partial, and the Trust page will list the sorry and axiom counts.
- **Licence:** this repository is under the [MIT License](https://github.com/tangentproofs/vau-calculus/blob/main/LICENSE). The cited works keep their own copyright. This site quotes only short, attributed phrases and does not copy the thesis.
- **Corrections:** open an issue or pull request on [tangentproofs/vau-calculus](https://github.com/tangentproofs/vau-calculus), or comment on any node.
